business_context.audience: Small independent design studios onboarding a first retainer client
business_context.brand_position: A simple notes/checklist concept; positioning untested
business_context.business_problem: Studio owners already understand onboarding but cannot tell whether the notes/checklist concept fits their handoff process.
business_context.candidate_scope: Controlled five-keyword comparison; no padding or live expansion.
business_context.competitive_position: May compete with spreadsheets; no competitive research supplied
business_context.constraints: No real integrations, pricing, security or outcomes claims
business_context.conversion_definition: Completed walkthrough-request submission, measured as a unique submitted request; no conversion rate or predicted lift supplied.
business_context.evidence_notice: All business context is synthetic, positioning untested; reserved-domain result fixtures are not Google observations.
business_context.objective_tradeoffs: Prioritize fit assessment and an accurately described walkthrough request over broad introductory traffic.
business_context.resources: Three candidate briefs only; no article writer, deployment, or publication authorized.
business_context.website_stage: Fictional new site; no measurement history

editorial.differentiation: Fit-screening from the stated conversion problem, rather than a general onboarding tutorial. S2 has not been content-audited and cannot establish a competitor gap.
evidence_needed: Human studio-operator review of the proposed workflow
Actual product capability verification before factual product claims
Current comparable real Google top-ten evidence and page-content audit for SEO conclusions
key_points: Reader job: an already-informed owner identifies whether the fictional notes/checklist concept deserves further evaluation; introductory category education is secondary (S1).
Provide a requirement / evidence available / unanswered question decision table. Only notes and checklists are supplied concept facts; integrations, permissions and automation are unknown.
Next action: request a workflow walkthrough only if the concept matches the basic need; the request is not a promise of suitability or a completed purchase.
Measurement: the defined event is a unique completed walkthrough-request submission. A click is not completion; no baseline, conversion rate or lift is known.
Acceptance: include a clear not-yet-verified requirements list and an alternative next step for readers who need unsupported capabilities.
editorial.meta_description: Test your studio’s handoff needs against a notes-and-checklist workflow, identify unanswered requirements and decide whether to request a walkthrough.
outline: H2: Define the handoff you need to improve
H2: Fit test — can notes and a checklist represent the required inputs and owners?
H3: Identify requirements that need verification, including approvals and access controls
H2: Bring one representative workflow to a walkthrough
H2: Decide whether to request a walkthrough or investigate another approach
editorial.reader_job: Reader job: an already-informed owner identifies whether the fictional notes/checklist concept deserves further evaluation; introductory category education is secondary (S1).
editorial.title: Use a client onboarding checklist to assess your workflow fit

editorial.differentiation: The conversion context turns comparison into a requirements-and-proof handoff. It does not justify persuasion based on unsupported product benefits.
evidence_needed: Human studio-operator review of the proposed workflow
Actual product capability verification before factual product claims
Current comparable real Google top-ten evidence and page-content audit for SEO conclusions
key_points: Reader job: make a conditional fit decision, not select a universally best platform.
Comparison matrix columns: requirement, supplied evidence, verification question, blocker status. Do not fill missing capability cells with inferred yes/no answers.
Request a walkthrough only after identifying a plausible fit and unresolved questions worth testing.
Acceptance: exact event is completed request submission; do not invent form availability, prices, integrations, competitor weaknesses, or improved conversion outcomes.
editorial.meta_description: Prepare a requirements-led comparison and verify unknown capabilities before deciding whether the MossNote concept merits a walkthrough.
outline: H2: Establish must-have workflow requirements
H2: Separate supplied concept facts from unanswered capability questions
H3: Notes and checklists are the stated concept; other capabilities need evidence
H2: Ask vendors to demonstrate a representative handoff
H2: Record fit, unresolved risks and the next decision
editorial.reader_job: Reader job: make a conditional fit decision, not select a universally best platform.
editorial.title: Client onboarding software comparison: a fit checklist for your walkthrough
